note: Every element of docs/contract.json is derived from the single pinned OpenAPI specification recorded below. No rendered documentation page, product guide, API Explorer view, or blog post is a contract source.

specification.commit_note: Commit c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba is the 'VCF API Specs 9.1 release readiness' revision that published the 9.1.0.0 specifications. This is the sibling specification to specifications/vcf-operations/log-management-openapi.json; log management is a different API and is not a source for this contract.

operations.purpose: Exchange a username, password and optional auth source for the token that authorizes every subsequent call.
derived_facts: security is declared as [] on this operation, so it is the only unauthenticated operation in the projection

operations.purpose: Report the product version of the server that the session is bound to.
List the notification plugin types the server supports, so an unsupported pluginTypeId is rejected before anything is created.
derived_facts: the operation declares no parameters and no request body
alert-plugin-types carries the supported identifiers in the notificationPluginType string array

operations.purpose: Create an outbound alert (notification) plugin instance; the server assigns its pluginId.
derived_facts: 201 is the only declared response status
the created pluginId is returned in the response body, not in a Location header

operations.purpose: Resolve a payload template by name so the notification rule can reference its templateId.
derived_facts: every declared query parameter is optional: name, description, outboundMethod, modifiedBy, page, pageSize
page defaults to 0 and pageSize defaults to 1000 server-side, so neither has to be transmitted
the operation declares no request body

operations.purpose: Bind a notification rule to an existing plugin instance and payload template.
derived_facts: 404 and 422 are declared alongside 201, so a rejected rule is an expected outcome rather than a transport fault
the projection names no delete or update operation, so a rejected rule leaves any plugin created earlier in place

supporting_schemas.name: username-password
derived_facts: required: [username, password]
authSource is optional

supporting_schemas.name: auth-token
derived_facts: required: [token, validity]
validity is integer/int64 milliseconds since Jan 1 1970
expiresAt and roles are optional

supporting_schemas.name: version
derived_facts: required: [humanlyReadableReleaseDate, major, minor, minorMinor, releaseName, releasedDate]
patch, buildNumber and description are optional

supporting_schemas.name: alert-plugin-types
derived_facts: no required properties
notificationPluginType is an array of plain strings, not of objects

supporting_schemas.name: notification-plugin
derived_facts: required: [name, pluginTypeId]
description, configValues, certificates, pluginId and enabled are all optional
enabled is documented as a read-only property whose value is set by the system, so a client must not send it on create
pluginId is documented as needed only during update operations

supporting_schemas.name: name-value
derived_facts: required: [name, value]
both properties are strings

supporting_schemas.name: notification-templates
derived_facts: notificationTemplates, pageInfo and links are all optional, so an empty result may omit the array entirely

supporting_schemas.name: notification-template
derived_facts: required: [name, pluginTypeId]
templateId is optional and is the value a notification rule references
templateType draws from the ALERT, ACTION, UNKNOWN enum

supporting_schemas.name: notification-rule
derived_facts: required: [name, pluginId]
pluginId is typed as a plain string here, unlike notification-plugin.pluginId which is a uuid-formatted string
templateId, criticalities, alertStatuses, alertControlStates, collectorGroupId, enabled, sendHeartbeat, ruleType and every filter collection are optional
enabled defaults to true and sendHeartbeat defaults to false server-side, so neither has to be transmitted
id is assigned by the system on create
resourceFilter and resourceKindFilter are documented as deprecated in favour of resourceFilters and resourceKindFilters

supporting_schemas.name: criticality
derived_facts: enum: [UNKNOWN, NONE, INFORMATION, WARNING, IMMEDIATE, CRITICAL, AUTO]
the collection has uniqueItems: true

security_schemes.name: Token-based-authorization
derived_facts: type: apiKey, in: header, name: Authorization
the token value acquired from acquireToken is presented with the OpsToken prefix
